verses.zh: 他对我说：「人子啊，要吃你所得的，要吃这书卷，好去对以色列家讲说。」
verses.en: He said to me, “Son of man, eat what you see in front of you[NOTE:1]—eat this scroll—and then go and speak to the house of Israel.”
notes: Heb “eat what you find.”
verses.commentary:
3:1 "Son of man" See note at Ezek. 2:1.

verses.zh: 于是我开口，他就使我吃这书卷，
verses.en: So I opened my mouth and he fed me the scroll.

verses.zh: 又对我说：「人子啊，要吃我所赐给你的这书卷，充满你的肚腹。」我就吃了，口中觉得其甜如蜜。
verses.en: He said to me, “Son of man, feed your stomach and fill your belly with this scroll I am giving to you.” So I ate it,[NOTE:1] and it was sweet like honey in my mouth.
notes: Heb “I ate,” a first common singular preterite plus paragogic he (ה). The ancient versions read “I ate it,” which is certainly the meaning in the context, and indicates they read the he as a third feminine singular pronominal suffix. The Masoretes typically wrote a mappiq in the he for the pronominal suffix but apparently missed this one.sn I ate it. A similar idea of consuming God’s word is found in Jer 15:16 and Rev 10:10, where it is also compared to honey and may be specifically reminiscent of this text.
verses.commentary:
3:3 "Then I ate it, and it was sweet as honey to my mouth" This conveys the thought that YHWH's word is significant
and meaningful even when it is a message of judgment (cf. Ps. 19:10; 119:103; Jer. 15:16; Rev. 10:9, 10). That the Holy Creator
God would be involved with sinful humanity is amazing! God's judgment is really a sign of His parental discipline (cf. Heb. 12:5-13).

verses.zh: 他对我说：「人子啊，你往以色列家那里去，将我的话对他们讲说。
verses.en: He said to me, “Son of man, go to the house of Israel and speak my words to them.

verses.zh: 你奉差遣不是往那说话深奥、言语难懂的民那里去，乃是往以色列家去；
verses.en: For you are not being sent to a people of unintelligible speech[NOTE:1] and difficult language,[NOTE:2] but[NOTE:3] to the house of Israel—
notes: Heb “deep of lip” (in the sense of incomprehensible).
Heb “heavy of tongue.” Similar language occurs in Exod 4:10 and Isa 33:19.
The conjunction “but” is not in the Hebrew text but is implied from the context.

verses.zh: 不是往那说话深奥、言语难懂的多国去，他们的话语是你不懂得的。我若差你往他们那里去，他们必听从你。
verses.en: not to many peoples of unintelligible speech and difficult language, whose words you cannot understand.[NOTE:1] Surely if[NOTE:2] I had sent you to them, they would listen to you!
notes: Heb “hear.”
The MT reads: “if not,” but most ancient versions translate only “if.” The expression occurs with this sense in Isa 5:9 and 14:24. See also Ezek 34:8; 36:5; 38:19.

verses.zh: 以色列家却不肯听从你，因为他们不肯听从我；原来以色列全家是额坚心硬的人。
verses.en: But the house of Israel is unwilling to listen to you,[NOTE:1] because they are not willing to listen to me,[NOTE:2] for the whole house of Israel is hardheaded and hardhearted.[NOTE:3]
notes: Moses (Exod 3:19) and Isaiah (Isa 6:9-10) were also told that their messages would not be received.
A similar description of Israel’s disobedience is given in 1 Sam 8:7.
Heb “hard of forehead and stiff of heart.”
verses.commentary:
3:7 "the whole house of Israel is stubborn and obstinate" See note at Ezek. 2:4. They will not listen to Moses
or the Prophets (i.e. 20:8; Isa. 6:9-13).

SPECIAL TOPIC: STUBBORNNESS (OT)

verses.zh: 看哪，我使你的脸硬过他们的脸，使你的额硬过他们的额。
verses.en: “I have made your face adamant[NOTE:1] to match their faces, and your forehead hard to match their foreheads.
notes: Heb “strong, resolute.”

verses.zh: 我使你的额像金钢钻，比火石更硬。他们虽是悖逆之家，你不要怕他们，也不要因他们的脸色惊惶。」
verses.en: I have made your forehead harder than flint—like diamond![NOTE:1] Do not fear them or be terrified of the looks they give you,[NOTE:2] for they are a rebellious house.”
notes: The Hebrew term translated “diamond” is parallel to “iron” in Jer 17:1. The Hebrew uses two terms which are both translated at times as “flint,” but here one is clearly harder than the other. The translation “diamond” attempts to reflect this distinction in English.
Heb “of their faces.”
verses.commentary:
3:9

NASB
"emery"

NKJV, JPSOA, REB, Peshitta
"adamant stone"

NRSV
"the hardest stone"

TEV
"as firm as rock"

NJB
"a diamond"

This Hebrew root (BDB 1038) has several meanings.

- thorns, briars, only in Isaiah (cf. Ezek. 5:6; 7:23,24,25; 9:18; 10:17; 27:4; 32:13)

- adamant, flint (i.e. hard stone), Jer. 17:1; Ezek. 3:9; Zech. 7:12

- person's name, 1 Chr. 24:24

- place name, Josh. 15:48; Jdg. 10:1,2

Context determines meaning! Only #2 fits. Which hard stone is being referenced is uncertain.

▣ "Do not be afraid of them or be dismayed before them" See note at Ezek. 2:6.

verses.zh: 他又对我说：「人子啊，我对你所说的一切话，要心里领会，耳中听闻。
verses.en: And he said to me, “Son of man, take all my words that I speak to you to heart and listen carefully.
verses.commentary:
3:10 What an insight into how inspiration worked in this case. The prophet had to listen (i.e. eat the scroll,
cf. Ezek. 2:8), receive (i.e. comprehend), and then speak the message to the exiled tribes in Babylon.

verses.zh: 你往你本国被掳的子民那里去，他们或听，或不听，你要对他们讲说，告诉他们这是主耶和华说的。」
verses.en: Go to the exiles, to your fellow countrymen,[NOTE:1] and speak to them. Say to them, ‘This is what the Sovereign Lord says,’ whether they pay attention or not.”
notes: Heb “to the sons of your people.”
verses.commentary:
3:11 "go to the exiles" This is the specific group that Ezekiel is commissioned to speak YHWH's message to,
the exiled tribes in Babylon.

▣ "whether they listen or not" Some will respond, but others will not (note the parable of the soils,
Matt. 13:1-15; Mark 4:1-12; Luke 8:4-10). There has always been a spiritual divide within national Israel. Some are covenant
people by lineage only, but others are trusting, obeying, and heart-felt covenant followers!

SPECIAL TOPIC: LISTEN/HEAR (shema)

SPECIAL TOPIC: REMNANT (three senses)

verses.zh: 那时，灵将我举起，我就听见在我身后有震动轰轰的声音，说：「从耶和华的所在显出来的荣耀是该称颂的！」
verses.en: Then a wind lifted me up[NOTE:1] and I heard a great rumbling sound behind me as the glory of the Lord rose from its place,[NOTE:2]
notes: See note on “wind” in 2:2.

This translation accepts the emendation suggested in BHS of בְּרוּם (berum, “in the lifting”) for בָּרוּךְ (barukh). The letters mem (מ) and kaf (כ) were easily confused in the old script, while בָּרוּךְ (“blessed be”) implies a quotation, which is out of place here. The word also does not fit the later phrase “from its place,” which requires a verb of motion.
verses.commentary:
3:12 "the Spirit lifted me up" There is some doubt about to whom "spirit" refers in Ezek. 1:12,20,21 (there is no DEFINITE ARTICLE),
but here and in Ezek. 2:2 it obviously refers to the active presence of God. It may be true that a full-blown Trinitarian understanding of God is absent
from the OT. There are still texts (such as this one) that point toward a plurality in God (see SPECIAL TOPIC: THE TRINITY, II.).

There are several places in Ezekiel where this phrase is used implying that it is a literary way of introducing revelation
(cf. Ezek. 2:2; 3:12,14,24; 8:3; 11:1,24; 37:1; 43:5). Ezekiel is receiving active, personal revelation in the form of visions and words.

SPECIAL TOPIC: BREATH, WIND, SPIRIT

SPECIAL TOPIC: PERSONHOOD OF THE SPIRIT

SPECIAL TOPIC: SPIRIT IN THE BIBLE

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE TRINITY, II. C.

This NOUN (BDB 950, KB 1272) can refer to

- the sound of an earthquake, 1 Kgs. 19:11-12; Ezek. 38:19; Amos 1:1; Zech. 14:5

- the context of a loud voice, Isa. 29:6

- the sound of military action

- warriors, Isa. 9:4

- war chariots, Jer. 10:22; 47:3

- war horses, Job 39:24

- the shaking of persons, Ezek. 12:18

- the VERB is used often of divine comings for judgment or blessing

In this context (cf. Ezek. 3:13) it was the sound of YHWH's throne chariot lifting up and moving.
Somehow the "lifting up" of the Spirit is equated with the lifting up of the throne chariot (cf. Ezek. 1:12,20-21).
With the sound of the movement of the throne chariot was a vocal statement of the attending angelic being, "Blessed
by the glory of the Lord in/from His place." This is similar to the Seraphim of Isa. 6:3.

Ezekiel heard a sound (vv. 12-13) and saw an event, just before the Spirit carried him away.

▣ "glory" SPECIAL TOPIC: GLORY (kabod, OT)

verses.zh: 我又听见那活物翅膀相碰，与活物旁边轮子旋转震动轰轰的响声。
verses.en: and the sound of the living beings’ wings brushing against each other, and the sound of the wheels alongside them, a great rumbling sound.

verses.zh: 于是灵将我举起，带我而去。我心中甚苦，灵性忿激，并且耶和华的灵（原文是手）在我身上大有能力。
verses.en: A wind lifted me up and carried me away. I went bitterly,[NOTE:1] my spirit full of fury, and the hand of the Lord rested powerfully[NOTE:2] on me.
notes: The traditional interpretation is that Ezekiel embarked on his mission with bitterness and anger, either reflecting God’s attitude toward the sinful people or his own feelings about having to carry out such an unpleasant task. L. C. Allen (Ezekiel [WBC], 1:13) takes “bitterly” as a misplaced marginal note and understands the following word, normally translated “anger,” in the sense of fervor or passion. He translates, “I was passionately moved” (p. 4). Another option is to take the word translated “bitterly” as a verb meaning “strengthened” (attested in Ugaritic). See G. R. Driver, Canaanite Myths and Legends, 152.

Heb “the hand of the Lord was on me heavily.” The “hand of the Lord” is a metaphor for his power or influence; the modifier conveys intensity. sn In Ezekiel God’s “hand” being on the prophet is regularly associated with communication or a vision from God (1:3; 3:14, 22; 8:1; 37:1; 40:1).
verses.commentary:
3:14 "and I went embittered in rage of my spirit" This is a very difficult phrase. It has been translated in
one of two ways:

- Ezekiel is upset at having to give a hard message which will be rejected

- Ezekiel was filled with the righteous indignation of God at the sin of the Jewish nation (cf. Jer. 6:11)

I think theory 2 fits the context much better.

▣ "the hand of the Lord" Notice the different ways the presence of
YHWH is alluded to.

- direct speech, Ezek. 3:1,4,16,24,27

- the Spirit, Ezek. 3:12,14,24

- the glory of the Lord, Ezek. 3:12,23 (see SPECIAL TOPIC: GLORY [OT])

- the hand of the Lord, Ezek. 3:14,22 (see
SPECIAL TOPIC: HAND)

The anthropomorphic imagery denotes the reception of divine revelation (cf. Ezek. 1:3; 3:14,22; 8:1; 33:22;
37:1; 40:1).

SPECIAL TOPIC: GOD DESCRIBED AS HUMAN (anthropomorphism).

verses.zh: 我就来到提勒・亚毕，住在迦巴鲁河边被掳的人那里，到他们所住的地方，在他们中间忧忧闷闷地坐了七日。
verses.en: I came to the exiles at Tel Abib,[NOTE:1] who lived by the Kebar River.[NOTE:2] I sat dumbfounded among them there, where they were living, for seven days.[NOTE:3]
notes: The name “Tel Abib” is a transliteration of an Akkadian term meaning “mound of the flood,” i.e., an ancient mound. It is not to be confused with the modern city of Tel Aviv in Israel.
Or “canal.”
A similar response to a divine encounter is found in Acts 9:8-9.
verses.commentary:
3:15 "Tel-abib" This is also the name of one of the Canaanite months, which was the month of the Exodus/Passover.
Here it is a settlement by the Grand Canal close to the city of Nippur.

The Hebrew word abib (BDB 1) means "green ears of grain." "Tel" (BDB 1068) means "mound."

SPECIAL TOPIC: ANE CALENDARS

NASB
"I sat there seven days where they were living,

causing consternation among them"

NKJV, Peshitta
"I sat where they sat, and remained there

astonished among them seven days"

NRSV, JPSOA
"I sat there among them, stunned for seven

days"

TEV
"I came. . .and for seven days I stayed there,

overcome by what I had seen and heard"

NJB
"I came. . .and there I stayed with them

in a stupor for seven days"

LXX
"I sat there seven days, conversant in the

midst of them"

The Hebrew VERB (BDB 1030, KB 1563, Hiphil PARTICIPLE)
means "appalled," "awestruck," "devastated." But to whom does it refer?

- Ezekiel (i.e. the vision itself), NKJV, NRSV, TEV, NJB, JPSOA

- the exiled Israelites of Tel-abib (i.e. the message of Ezekiel), LXX, NASB

Just an added thought. The time of "seven days" may be related to a designated "ordination" period
for priests (cf. Exod. 29:35-37; Lev. 8:33-35); if so, then option #1 above seems best, but it does not explain the VERB.

verses.zh: 过了七日，耶和华的话临到我说：
verses.en: At the end of seven days the Lord’s message came to me:

verses.zh: 「人子啊，我立你作以色列家守望的人，所以你要听我口中的话，替我警戒他们。
verses.en: “Son of man, I have appointed you a watchman[NOTE:1] for the house of Israel. Whenever you hear a word from my mouth, you must give them a warning from me.
notes: The literal role of a watchman is described in 2 Sam 18:24 and 2 Kgs 9:17.
verses.commentary:
3:17 "I have appointed you a watchman" This is expanded in Ezekiel 33. It is a concept used often in the
prophets (cf. Isa. 56:10; Jer. 6: 17; Hosea 9:8). Remember the prophets functioned as YHWH's covenant enforcers
for the Mosaic covenant. Israel's obedience determined her destiny. The prophets reminded Israel of the
consequences of disobedience (cf. Leviticus 26; Deuteronomy 28). How the people responded to the prophets'
message (i.e. repentance or hardness) determined their future.

SPECIAL TOPIC: PROPHECY (OT)

verses.zh: 我何时指着恶人说：他必要死；你若不警戒他，也不劝戒他，使他离开恶行，拯救他的性命，这恶人必死在罪孽之中；我却要向你讨他丧命的罪（原文是血）。
verses.en: When I say to the wicked, ‘You will certainly die,’[NOTE:1] and you do not warn him—you do not speak out to warn the wicked to turn from his wicked lifestyle so that he may live—that wicked person will die for his iniquity,[NOTE:2] but I will hold you accountable for his death.[NOTE:3]
notes: Even though the infinitive absolute is used to emphasize the warning, the warning is still implicitly conditional, as the following context makes clear.

Or “in his punishment.” The phrase “in/for [a person’s] iniquity” occurs fourteen times in Ezekiel: here and v. 19; 4:17; 7:13, 16; 18:17, 18, 19, 20; 24:23; 33:6, 8, 9; 39:23. The Hebrew word for “iniquity” may also mean the “punishment for iniquity.”
Heb “his blood I will seek from your hand.” The expression “seek blood from the hand” is equivalent to requiring the death penalty (2 Sam 4:11-12).
verses.commentary:
3:18-19 This is a major theological truth of both Jeremiah and Ezekiel, which deals with individual responsibility for
spiritual choices. The full theological discussion is in Ezekiel 18 and 33.

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT

3:18 "You shall surely die" This is a Qal INFINITIVE ABSOLUTE and
a Qal IMPERFECT of the same VERB (BDB 559, KB 562),
which denotes emphasis. In this setting it refers to physical death. This same phrase occurs in Gen. 2:17!
Disobedience has consequences in time and eternity!

SPECIAL TOPIC: KEEP

SPECIAL TOPIC: WHERE ARE THE DEAD?

▣ "but his blood I will require at your hand" Being called to serve God is a great honor, but it also
carries great responsibilities. If I know God's message and do not speak, it brings spiritual consequences, as does
ignoring the message once given (cf. Ezek. 3:20; 33:6,8).

The term "blood" (BDB 196) is imagery of death. The ancients knew that as the blood flowed away,
so too, life. Therefore, the life was in the blood (cf. Gen. 9:5-6; Lev. 17:11,14).

SPECIAL TOPIC: BLOOD

verses.zh: 倘若你警戒恶人，他仍不转离罪恶，也不离开恶行，他必死在罪孽之中，你却救自己脱离了罪。
verses.en: But as for you, if you warn the wicked and he does not turn from his wicked deed and from his wicked lifestyle, he will die for his iniquity but you will have saved your own life.[NOTE:1]
notes: Verses 17-19 are repeated in Ezek 33:7-9.

verses.zh: 再者，义人何时离义而犯罪，我将绊脚石放在他面前，他就必死；因你没有警戒他，他必死在罪中，他素来所行的义不被记念；我却要向你讨他丧命的罪（原文是血）。
verses.en: “When a righteous person turns from his righteousness and commits iniquity, and I set an obstacle[NOTE:1] before him, he will die. If you have not warned him, he will die for his sin. The righteous deeds he performed will not be considered, but I will hold you accountable for his death.
notes: Or “stumbling block.” The Hebrew term refers to an obstacle in the road in Lev 19:14.
verses.commentary:
3:20 "a righteous man" See SPECIAL TOPIC: RIGHTEOUSNESS

▣ "I place an obstacle before him" God tests all those who belong to Him (cf. Gen. 22:1; Exod. 15:25;
16:4; 20:20; Deut. 8:2,16; 13:3; Jdg. 2:22; 2 Chr. 32:31; Matt. 4:1; Heb. 12:5-13).

Ezekiel uses the imagery of a stone or obstacle placed on the road (i.e. life's path) as a way of
denoting judgment (cf. Jer. 6:21). The fact that God tests humans demands that humans have a God-given "free will"
(cf. Gen. 1:26-27). If there is no personal responsibility there can be no ethical consequences! The interpersonal
relationship desired by God of His human creatures demands a free will.

Ezekiel also emphasizes an individual aspect to faith and obedience that is unique in the prophets
who usually address national Israel (cf. Ezek. 3:20-21; 14:12-20; 18:5-32; 33:12-20).

SPECIAL TOPIC: GOD TESTS HIS PEOPLE

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE PATH, THE WAY

verses.zh: 倘若你警戒义人，使他不犯罪，他就不犯罪；他因受警戒就必存活，你也救自己脱离了罪。」
verses.en: However, if you warn the righteous person not to sin, and he[NOTE:1] does not sin, he will certainly live because he was warned, and you will have saved your own life.”
notes: Heb “the righteous man.”

verses.zh: 耶和华的灵（原文是手）在那里降在我身上。他对我说：「你起来往平原去，我要在那里和你说话。」
verses.en: The hand[NOTE:1] of the Lord rested on me there, and he said to me, “Get up, go out to the valley,[NOTE:2] and I will speak with you there.”
notes: Or “power.” sn Hand in the OT can refer metaphorically to power, authority, or influence. In Ezekiel God’s hand being on the prophet is regularly associated with communication or a vision from God (1:3; 3:14, 22; 8:1; 37:1; 40:1).
Ezekiel had another vision at this location, recounted in Ezek 37.
verses.commentary:
3:22 "The hand of the Lord" See notes at Ezek. 3:14.

SPECIAL TOPIC: HAND

▣ This is similar to Ezek. 2:1. YHWH is initiating contact and preparing to communicate revelation.

- "Arise," BDB 877, KB 1086, Qal IMPERATIVE

- "Go out," BDB 422, KB 425, Qal IMPERATIVE

- "I will speak to you," BDB 180, KB 210, Piel IMPERFECT

verses.zh: 于是我起来往平原去，不料，耶和华的荣耀正如我在迦巴鲁河边所见的一样，停在那里，我就俯伏于地。
verses.en: So I got up and went out to the valley, and the glory of the Lord was standing there, just like the glory I had seen by the Kebar River,[NOTE:1] and I threw myself face down.
notes: Or “canal.”
verses.commentary:
3:23 "I got up and went out on the plain and behold the glory of the Lord was
standing there" This experience was a major theological revelation. God's glory and presence were not limited to
Palestine or the temple (i.e. Acts 7). The exiles needed to know this. He is the God of all the earth, of all creation!

- that God had not abandoned them

- that God was not limited to the Holy Land

Notice how "glory" is personified as "standing." The term "glory" stands for the personal presence of YHWH.

SPECIAL TOPIC: GLORY (kabod, OT)

verses.zh: 灵就进入我里面，使我站起来。耶和华对我说：「你进房屋去，将门关上。
verses.en: Then a wind[NOTE:1] came into me and stood me on my feet. The Lord[NOTE:2] spoke to me and said, “Go shut yourself in your house.
notes: See the note on “wind” in 2:2.
Heb “he.”
verses.commentary:
3:24 "The Spirit then entered me" This is the same "spirit" that controlled the living being of chapter 1
(cf. Ezek. 1:12,20-21). It is the same "spirit" that entered Ezekiel and caused him to stand in Ezek. 2:1-2. It is a
way of referring to God Himself. Notice "He spoke with me" and the obvious antecedent is "the Spirit."

The Spirit of God is active in the OT in equipping humans to perform divine tasks or assignments.

- design and building of the tabernacle, Exod. 31:3; 35:31

- military deliverers, Jdg. 6:34; 11:29; 13:25; 14:6,19; 15:14

- political leaders, 1 Sam. 10:10; 11:6; 16:13; 2 Sam. 23:2

- prophets, 1 Kgs. 18:12,46; 2 Kgs. 2:16; Ezek. 2:2; 3:12,14,24; 8:3; 11:24; 37:1; 43:5; Micah 3:5

SPECIAL TOPIC: SPIRIT IN THE BIBLE

▣ "Go, shut yourself up in your house" Notice how specific God's message is. Ezekiel is claiming that
his dramatic acts are direct commands from YHWH.

- "go," BDB 97, KB 112, Qal IMPERATIVE

- "be shut up," BDB 688, KB 742, Niphal IMPERATIVE

verses.zh: 人子啊，人必用绳索捆绑你，你就不能出去在他们中间来往。
verses.en: As for you, son of man, they will put ropes on you and tie you up with them, so you cannot go out among them.
verses.commentary:
3:25 The question is, who does the PRONOUN "they" refer to?

- other exiles

- the Babylonian army besieging Jerusalem (cf. Ezek. 4:8)

Whatever the exact meaning, it is clear from the context that there will be opposition to Ezekiel's
message (cf. Ezek. 3:26-27). Ezekiel is declaring the complete destruction of Jerusalem and the temple and the exile,
which was not a popular message (i.e. Jeremiah's message).

verses.zh: 我必使你的舌头贴住上膛，以致你哑口，不能作责备他们的人；他们原是悖逆之家。
verses.en: I will make your tongue stick to the roof of your mouth so that you will be silent and unable to reprove[NOTE:1] them, for they are a rebellious house.
notes: Heb “you will not be to them a reprover.” In Isa 29:21 and Amos 5:10 “a reprover” issued rebuke at the city gate.
verses.commentary:
3:26 "I will make your tongue stick to the roof of your mouth" In context this is highly unusual, since God
is commanding him to tell the message, but it may communicate the truth that the prophet is only to speak when God speaks. There
will be a specific content and time to speak (cf. Ezek. 24:27; 33:22). This reference to a divine silence is seen again in Ezek. 24:27: 29:21; 33:22.

verses.zh: 但我对你说话的时候，必使你开口，你就要对他们说：『主耶和华如此说。』听的可以听，不听的任他不听，因为他们是悖逆之家。」
verses.en: But when I speak with you, I will loosen your tongue[NOTE:1] and you must say to them, ‘This is what the Sovereign Lord says.’ Those who listen will listen, but the indifferent will refuse,[NOTE:2] for they are a rebellious house.
notes: Heb “open your mouth.”

Heb “the listener will listen, and the refuser will refuse.” Because the word for listening can also mean obeying, the nuance may be that the obedient will listen, or that the one who listens will obey. Also, although the verbs are not jussive as pointed in the MT, some translate them with a volitive sense: “the one who listens—let that one listen, the one who refuses—let that one refuse.”
verses.commentary:
3:27 This verse concludes with two commands.

- "let him hear," BDB 1033, KB 1570, Qal IMPERFECT used
in a JUSSIVE sense

- "let him refuse" (lit. "cease"), BDB 292, KB 292, Qal IMPERFECT used
in a JUSSIVE sense
